examples.solution_text:
Read the points $(0,20)$ and $(8,60)$. The volume increases by $40$ L in $8$ minutes.
$\begin{align*}\text{Filling rate}&=\frac{60-20}{8-0}\\&=5\text{ L/min}\end{align*}$
The tank starts with $20$ L. In $12$ minutes it gains $5\times12=60$ L.
$\begin{align*}\text{Volume at 12 minutes}&=20+60\\&=80\text{ L}\end{align*}$

Read the points $(0,120)$ and $(6,60)$.
$\begin{align*}m&=\frac{60-120}{6-0}\\m&=-10\text{ L/min}\end{align*}$
The negative gradient shows decreasing volume. The rate of decrease is $10$ L/min.
The tank must lose its starting volume of $120$ L to become empty.
$\begin{align*}\text{Time to empty}&=\frac{120}{10}\\&=12\text{ minutes}\end{align*}$

Use the endpoints of each straight section.
From $0$ to $4$ seconds, volume rises from $0$ to $40$ L.
$\begin{align*}\text{First rate}&=\frac{40-0}{4-0}\\&=10\text{ L/s}\end{align*}$
From $4$ to $6$ seconds, volume stays at $40$ L. The horizontal section has a filling rate of $0$ L/s.
From $6$ to $12$ seconds, volume rises from $40$ to $60$ L.
$\begin{align*}\text{Final rate}&=\frac{60-40}{12-6}\\&=\frac{10}{3}\text{ L/s}\end{align*}$
The final interval lasts $6$ seconds; it excludes the pause.

The second stage starts at $(4,60)$ and ends at $(10,30)$. The tank loses $30$ L over $6$ minutes.
$\begin{align*}\text{Rate of decrease}&=\frac{60-30}{10-4}\\&=5\text{ L/min}\end{align*}$

At $6$ minutes, hose A has delivered $15$ L and hose B has delivered $9$ L.
$\begin{align*}\text{Hose A rate}&=\frac{15}{6}\\&=2.5\text{ L/min}\end{align*}$
$\begin{align*}\text{Hose B rate}&=\frac{9}{6}\\&=1.5\text{ L/min}\end{align*}$
Hose A fills faster. Its line is steeper on the shared axes.

Read the starting volume of $30$ L and the volume of $120$ L at $6$ minutes.
$\begin{align*}\text{Filling rate}&=\frac{120-30}{6-0}\\&=15\text{ L/min}\end{align*}$
The tank needs another $180-30=150$ L.
$\begin{align*}\text{Time to reach capacity}&=\frac{150}{15}\\&=10\text{ minutes}\end{align*}$

examples.derivation: The graph's vertical scale is 10 L per grid interval, giving endpoints (0,20) and (8,60). The filling rate is (60-20)/(8-0)=5 L/min. Continuing for 12 minutes adds 5×12=60 L to the initial 20 L, giving 80 L. This follows the supplied gradient-and-extension method.
The plotted endpoints represent (0,120) and (6,60). Signed gradient = (60−120)/6 = −10 L/min; rate of decrease = 10 L/min. Emptying the initial 120 L takes 120/10 = 12 minutes.

The plotted vertices represent (0,0), (4,40), (6,40) and (12,60), with time in seconds and volume in litres. The first rate is 40/4=10 L/s. The pause has rate (40-40)/(6-4)=0 L/s. The final rate is (60-40)/(12-6)=20/6=10/3 L/s. Each calculation uses only its stage's endpoints.
The graph represents (0,90), (4,60) and (10,30). During the second stage, volume decreases by 60−30 = 30 L over 10−4 = 6 minutes. Rate of decrease = 30/6 = 5 L/min.

Both lines begin at (0,0). Hose A reaches (6,15), giving 15/6 = 2.5 L/min. Hose B reaches (6,9), giving 9/6 = 1.5 L/min. Hose A fills faster; its greater steepness is comparable because both lines share axes.
The endpoints represent (0,30) and (6,120). Filling rate = (120−30)/6 = 15 L/min. Reaching 180 L requires another 180−30 = 150 L, taking 150/15 = 10 minutes after t=0.
